chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If there is a deposit with you and you move (use) it, so upon you is the Zakat. But if you do not move (use) it, so there is nothing upon you.
ai.seo_question: When is Zakat obligatory on a deposit held for someone else?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'movement' (hark) in determining Zakat liability on deposits, distinguishing between wealth actively utilized by the holder versus that kept static. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights that the obligation often hinges on the owner's control and usage rather than mere possession, reflecting the nuanced application of Zakat on mixed or held assets. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how temporary custody interacts with the core conditions of Zakat eligibility.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If there was a deposit with you and you move (use) it, so upon you would be the Zakāt. But if you do not move (use) it, so there would be nothing upon you’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a certain asset is deposited with you and you are allowed to make it work its Zakat is on you but if you are not allowed to make it work then you do not owe anything.’”
